قَبْقَبٌ The belly; (S, M, O, K;) as also ↓ قَبْقَابٌ : (Suh, TA:) from ↓ قَبْقَبَةٌ , [an inf. n. of R. Q. 1, q. v., and] a word imitative of the sounding [or rumbling] of the belly. (TA.) ＝
-A2- And The wood of a horse's saddle: so in the saying, “يُطَيِّرُ الفَارِسُ لَوْ لَا قَبْقَبُهُ
” [He would make the horseman to fly off, were it not for the wood of his saddle]. (M. [But in this sense it is app. a mistranscription for قَيْقَبٌ.]) ―
-b2- And A species of trees; as also ↓ قَبْقَبَانٌ . (M. [But in this sense both are app. mistranscriptions, for قَيْقَبٌ and قَيْقَبَانٌ.])
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
